communityVoices.quote: The Playing> China Doll> Uncle John's Band is the clear high light of this show. It is excellent, full of energy with tight playing and lots of passion from Jerry.
communityVoices.attribution: Stellablu122, on the second set sequence

communityVoices.quote: Listen to the handoff of the second jam at just after the 5 minute mark. It'll break your heart. Phil is right there throughout as well. Just graceful sad stuff.
The Foolish Heart is intricate and you can hear Jerry not only tearing it up, but doing so WITH the band!
This Deer Creek run restored my faith after I saw some bad shows the previous 2 years. Phil was definitely in charge!
its my second dead show ever, also my first, um "paper experience" ever.

whyThisShow: This is one half of the two-night Deer Creek run released as Dave's Picks Vol. 40, and the community broadly regards it as the stronger night. One listener noted that "this show overall is a much better performance for Jerry than the previous night" and that "Phil is a beast the entire show". The second set's Playing in the Band sequence draws the most attention, with one reviewer calling it "excellent, full of energy with tight playing and lots of passion from Jerry". The Foolish Heart is singled out as a peak moment, one listener placing it in the "Top 3" for the song and hearing Jerry playing "WITH the band" rather than over it. One reviewer described the whole Deer Creek run as having "restored my faith after I saw some bad shows the previous 2 years".
listenFor: The Row Jimmy is the most cited individual moment — one listener zeroed in on "the handoff of the second jam at just after the 5 minute mark," calling it "graceful sad stuff" with Phil anchoring throughout. The Playing > Uncle John's Band sequence is the structural spine of the second set, described as carrying "lots of passion from Jerry" with "His solo in China Doll alone" cited as worth the listen. One reviewer also flagged Desolation Row as "flat out incredible" with Phil and Jerry both deeply engaged. Healy's mix draws a brief note — one listener loved his effects on Desolation Row while flagging a couple of moments where Weir gets run through the "screech box".
context: This show is from the summer 1990 tour, part of a two-night stand at Deer Creek Music Center in Noblesville, Indiana. It was officially released by the Dead's own archival series as Dave's Picks Vol. 40, paired with the July 18 show. The recording circulating on Archive.org is a soundboard (identifier: gd1990-07-19.sbd.miller.32354.sbeok.flac16). Brent Mydland died just days after this run, which gives the tape a particular weight for listeners who know the timeline — one reviewer noted of the Row Jimmy interplay, "It would all be over in a few days".
funFact: One reviewer described this as their second Dead show ever and their first "paper experience," writing "I would kill for a copy of this show".
headline: Deer Creek, July '90 — Brent's last run, officially out.
